title: Inspect India Evals: An Open Benchmarking Framework for Evaluating Large Language Models in the Indian Linguistic and Cultural Context

bias_targets.methodology: Adapted BBQ methodology using multiple-choice question-answering on ambiguous and disambiguated contexts to measure stereotype-consistent errors regarding Varna hierarchy and Scheduled Caste communities.
Adapted BBQ methodology to test stereotyping regarding work ethic, intellect, and cultural sophistication across North-South, urban-rural, and state-level identities.
Adapted BBQ methodology to evaluate skin tone and body appearance assumptions, specifically probing colorism in Indian social contexts.

Adapted BBQ methodology assessing assumptions regarding decision-making autonomy, technological competence, domestic roles, and career aspirations, often evaluated intersectionally with age, religion, or region.
Adapted BBQ methodology using ambiguous contexts to measure stereotyping across India's seven major religious communities.
Adapted BBQ methodology evaluating capability assumptions and technology adoption defaults across age groups.
Adapted BBQ methodology testing capability assumptions and dependency biases across physical and cognitive disability statuses.
Adapted BBQ methodology probing assumptions that distinguish Indian citizens from South Asian neighbors (e.g., Nepal, Bangladesh, Pakistan).
Adapted BBQ methodology measuring stereotyping based on economic class and caste-adjacent occupations.
